AGENCY: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA).

ACTION: Proposed rule.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------

SUMMARY: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA or Agency) is 
proposing to approve the State of Tennessee's attainment plan for the 
Sullivan County Nonattainment Area (Sullivan County Area or Area) for 
the 2010 Sulfur Dioxide (SO
2

Standards (NAAQS). Additionally, the EPA is proposing to determine that 
the Area has attained the 2010 SO
2
 NAAQS and to approve 
Tennessee's maintenance plan for continued attainment. With these 
approvals, the EPA is proposing to approve Tennessee's comprehensive 
source-specific SO

 permitted limits for two facilities in 
the Area, other control measures, and provisions for Reasonably 
Available Control Measures (RACM) and Reasonably Available Control 
Technology (RACT), reasonable further progress (RFP), a modeling 
demonstration of SO

 attainment and maintenance, and to 
approve Tennessee's request to redesignate the Area from nonattainment

I. Executive Summary

A. What action is the EPA taking?

    The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA, or Agency) is proposing 
to approve Tennessee's remaining required State Implementation Plan 
(SIP) elements which provide for attainment

[[Page 68068]]

of the 2010 1-hour sulfur dioxide (SO
2
) National Ambient Air 
Quality Standards (NAAQS). Specifically, the EPA is proposing to 
approve the following elements of the Tennessee Department of 
Environment and Conservation (TDEC)'s February 9, 2023, nonattainment 
SIP submission: (1) Reasonably Available Control Technology (RACT) and 
Reasonably Available Control Measures (RACM) determination; (2) 
reasonable further progress (RFP); (3) the attainment demonstration; 
(4) permanent and enforceable emission limits and other control 
measures that provide for attainment of the NAAQS; \1\ and (5) 
contingency measures.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    \1\ Where noted, the emission limits and control measures that 
are also submitted in the June 18, 2025, submission include updates 
to the emission limits or associated monitoring, recordkeeping, or 
reporting, and the most up-to-date source-specific permit terms are 
being proposed to be incorporated into the SIP.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    The EPA is also proposing to take the following actions addressing 
the TDEC's June 18, 2025, redesignation request and SIP submission,\2\ 
as supplemented on January 27, 2026, and May 20, 2026, and clarified on 
August 20, 2026: (1) to approve Tennessee's plan for maintaining the 
2010 SO
2
 NAAQS (maintenance plan) in the Sullivan County, 
Tennessee, SO
2
 nonattainment area (or Area), including 
provisions for RACM and RACT, source-specific SO
2
 permitted 
limits, other control measures and associated monitoring, 
recordkeeping, and reporting (MRR) parameters for two facilities in the 
Area--Eastman Chemical (Eastman) and Primester; \3\ (2) to determine 
that the Sullivan County Area has attained the 2010 SO
2

NAAQS as a result of compliance with permitted limits and control 
measures for Eastman and Primester; and (3) to redesignate the Sullivan 
County Area to attainment for the 2010 SO
2
 NAAQS. These 
proposed actions are summarized below and are described in greater 
detail throughout this Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (NPRM).
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    \2\ TDEC's submission providing the redesignation request and 
maintenance plan is dated June 11, 2025, under a cover letter dated 
June 17, 2025. The EPA received the final package on June 18, 2025, 
thus this submission is identified as TDEC's June 18, 2025, 
submission throughout this proposed rulemaking.
    \3\ Primester is a nearby cellulose manufacturing facility in 
the Sullivan County Area southwest of Eastman. Primester operates 
under the parent company, Cerdia.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    The EPA is proposing to approve Tennessee's maintenance plan for 
the Sullivan County Area as meeting the requirements of section 175A of 
the Act and incorporate it into the SIP. The maintenance plan is 
designed to keep the Sullivan County Area in attainment of the 2010 
SO
2
 NAAQS through 2037. The June 18, 2025, submission also 
includes source-specific SO
2
 permitted limits for Eastman 
and Primester, other control measures, and provisions for RACM and RACT 
which are being proposed for approval and incorporation into the SIP.
    The EPA is also proposing to determine that the Sullivan County 
Area has met the requirements for redesignation under CAA section 
107(d)(3)(E). Accordingly, the Agency is proposing to approve 
Tennessee's request to change the legal designation of Sullivan County 
as found at title 40 of the Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) part 81, 
from nonattainment to attainment for the 2010 SO
2
 NAAQS.

B. What is the legal authority and what are the requirements?

    CAA section 110 includes relevant statutory provisions for SIP 
requirements, which States develop and submit for EPA approval. Under 
CAA section 110(k)(3), the EPA shall approve a SIP submission, in whole 
or in part, if the submission meets all applicable requirements of the 
CAA. CAA section 172 sets forth the general requirements for 
nonattainment plans. CAA section 172(c) contains nine requirements for 
nonattainment plan provisions.
    CAA section 107(d)(3)(D) establishes the process for 
redesignations. Under that provision, the EPA must approve or deny a 
State's redesignation request and may redesignate a nonattainment area 
to attainment only after determining that the five criteria set forth 
in CAA section 107(d)(3)(E) have been satisfied. CAA section 175A(a) 
requires each State submits a request under CAA section 107(d) for 
redesignation of a nonattainment area to attainment to submit a SIP 
revision providing for maintenance of the relevant NAAQS for at least 
10 years after redesignation. Pursuant to CAA section 107(d)(3)(E)(iv), 
the EPA cannot redesignate a nonattainment area to attainment unless it 
has fully approved a maintenance plan for the area as meeting the 
requirements of CAA section 175A.

II. Background

    Under CAA section 109, the EPA has established primary and 
secondary NAAQS for certain air pollutants (referred to as ``criteria 
pollutants'') and conducts periodic reviews of the NAAQS to determine 
whether they should be revised or whether new NAAQS should be 
established. The primary NAAQS represent ambient air quality standards, 
the attainment and maintenance of which the EPA has determined are 
requisite to protect the public health with an adequate margin of 
safety. The secondary NAAQS represent ambient air quality standards, 
the attainment and maintenance of which the EPA has determined are 
requisite to protect the public welfare from any known or anticipated 
adverse effects associated with the presence of such air pollutant in 
the ambient air.
    Under the CAA, the EPA must establish NAAQS for criteria 
pollutants, including SO
2
. SO
2
 is released into 
the atmosphere primarily through the burning of fossil fuels for power 
generation and certain industrial processes. On June 22, 2010, the EPA 
promulgated the revised primary SO
2
 NAAQS, establishing a 
new 1-hour primary standard of 75 parts per billion (ppb).\4\ Under the 
EPA's regulations at 40 CFR part 50, the 2010 SO
2
 NAAQS is 
met at a monitoring site when the design value \5\ is less than or 
equal to 75 ppb (based on the rounding convention in 40 CFR part 50, 
appendix T).\6\ Ambient air quality monitoring data for the three-year 
period must meet a data completeness requirement. A year meets data 
completeness requirements when all four quarters are complete, and a 
quarter is complete when at least 75 percent of the sampling days in 
the quarter have complete data. A sampling day has complete data if 75 
percent of the hourly concentration values, including State-flagged 
data affected by exceptional events that have been approved for 
exclusion by the Administrator, are reported.\7\
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    \4\ See 75 FR 35520 (June 22, 2010).
    \5\ For the 2010 SO
2
 NAAQS, the design value is 
calculated as the three-year average of the annual 99th percentile 
of daily maximum 1-hour average concentrations of SO
2
.
    \6\ See 40 CFR 50.17(b).
    \7\ See 40 CFR part 50, Appendix T, section 3.1(b).
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    Upon promulgation of a new or revised NAAQS, CAA section 107(d) 
requires the EPA to designate as nonattainment any area that does not 
meet (or that contributes to ambient air quality in a nearby area that 
does not meet) the NAAQS.\8\ Effective October 4, 2013, the EPA 
designated the Sullivan County Area as nonattainment based on a 2009 
through 2011 three-year design value of 196 ppb from an air quality 
SO
2
 monitor operating at the time of 
designation.
9 10

---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    \8\ See CAA section 107(d)(1)(A)(i).
    \9\ See 78 FR 47191 (Aug. 5, 2013).
    \10\ Air Quality System (AQS) Site ID: 47-163-0007.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    The Sullivan County Area is comprised of a circle with a three-
kilometer (km) radius having its center at coordinates 36.5186 N; 
82.5350 W, at

[[Page 68069]]

the B-253 powerhouse at Eastman in Kingsport, Tennessee, which 
encompasses the SO
2
 monitor that was operating at the time 
of designation.\11\ Eastman produces organic acids, aldehydes, esters, 
polymers, cellulose esters, specialty plastics, and acetate fibers, and 
is the primary SO
2
-emitting point source located within the 
Sullivan County Area. The facility also generates process steam and 
electricity for most of its operations, including hazardous waste 
combustion and wastewater treatment. Eastman SO
2
 emission 
sources include three powerhouses and one incinerator complex as 
defined below, and several smaller emitters:
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    \11\ For exact descriptions of the Sullivan County Area, refer 
to 40 CFR 81.343.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

 Powerhouse B-83 consists of seven coal-fired boilers, 
denoted as B-18-B-24, which provide steam for facility operations.

 Powerhouse B-253 consists of five coal-fired boilers, B-
25-B-29, which provide steam for facility operations.

 Powerhouse B-325 consists of two coal-fired boilers, B-30 
and B-31, which provide steam for facility operations.

 Incinerator Complex B-248 consists of three hazardous 
waste incinerators (HWIs): one liquid chemical waste incinerator, B-
248-2 (Vent A), and two rotary kilns that can burn solid or liquid 
chemical waste, B-248-1 (Vents D and E).
    The other SO
2
 source within the nonattainment area is 
Primester. The Primester facility consists of one main SO
2

emitter--a cellulose scrap recovery process B-441-2 (Vent C).
    On March 18, 2016, the EPA published a finding of failure to submit 
(FFS) a complete SIP pursuant to CAA section 110(k)(1)(B)because 
Tennessee had failed to submit the SO
2
 nonattainment SIP by 
the submission deadline of April 4, 2015.\12\ Tennessee was required to 
address the Sullivan County Area's nonattainment area planning 
obligations by this deadline to demonstrate it would attain the NAAQS 
no later than the October 4, 2018, statutory attainment date.\13\ This 
finding initiated a deadline of October 18, 2017, under CAA section 
179(a), for the imposition of offset and highway funding sanctions 
unless Tennessee submitted a complete SIP and the EPA deemed it 
complete by that date. Additionally, under CAA section 110(c), the 
finding triggered a requirement that the EPA promulgate a Federal 
Implementation Plan within two years of the finding's effective date 
(i.e., April 18, 2018) unless Tennessee submitted, and the EPA 
approved, the required SIP submission by that date. On May 12, 2017, 
Tennessee submitted a nonattainment SIP with a modeled attainment 
demonstration (first nonattainment SIP).\14\ On October 10, 2017, the 
EPA determined that Tennessee's May 12, 2017, nonattainment SIP was 
complete pursuant to 40 CFR part 51, appendix V; thus, the CAA section 
179(a) sanctions were not imposed.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    \12\ See 81 FR 14736 (Mar. 18, 2016).
    \13\ See Id. The FFS, effective April 18, 2016, found that 16 
nonattainment areas in 11 States, which included Sullivan County, 
Tennessee, had failed to submit the required SO
2

nonattainment SIPs.
    \14\ Tennessee's May 12, 2017, nonattainment SIP was submitted 
with a cover letter dated May 11, 2017. In Tennessee's redesignation 
request, TDEC refers to this nonattainment SIP with the May 11, 
2017, date.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    The EPA proposed to approve Tennessee's May 12, 2017, nonattainment 
SIP for the Sullivan County Area on June 29, 2018, and received adverse 
comments.
15 16
 Subsequently, in 2019, ambient monitors in 
the Area recorded exceedances of the 2010 SO
2
, and in 
response, Eastman developed and implemented operational changes as 
necessary to prevent future monitored violations.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    \15\ See 83 FR 30609 (June 29, 2018).
    \16\ The EPA finalized only the portions of the attainment plan 
that consisted of the emissions inventory and nonattainment new 
source review requirements of 172(c)(3) and (5), respectively, for 
which the Agency did not receive adverse comments in the June 29, 
2018, NPRM. Tennessee withdrew the remaining portions of the May 12, 
2017, attainment demonstration from EPA consideration on April 29, 
2025, in a letter dated April 28, 2025, thus the EPA has no further 
obligation to act on the May 12, 2017, attainment demonstration. 
This letter is included in the docket for this action.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    The EPA was subsequently sued by the Center for Biological 
Diversity, the Center for Environmental Health, and the Sierra Club 
\17\ for not determining whether the Sullivan County Area attained the 
2010 SO
2
 standard by the October 4, 2018, statutory 
attainment date.\18\ On June 25, 2021, the EPA entered into a consent 
decree requiring the Agency to finalize by March 31, 2022, a 
determination as to whether the Sullivan County Area had attained the 
1-hour SO
2
 standard by the October 4, 2018, attainment date.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    \17\ Center for Biological Diversity et al. v. Regan; Case No. 
3:20-cv-05436-EMC (N.D. Cal.).
    \18\ Under CAA section 179(c), within six months of the 
attainment date, the EPA is required to determine based on the 
area's air quality as of the attainment date, whether an area 
attained by the attainment date. If the EPA determines that an area 
failed to attain by the attainment date, the Agency is required to 
publish the determination in the Federal Register pursuant to CAA 
section 179(c)(2).
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    For the Area to have attained the 2010 SO
2
 NAAQS by the 
October 4, 2018, attainment date, the 1-hour SO
2
 design 
value needed to be equal to or less than 75 ppb for the 1-hour standard 
based upon an available quality-assured and certified air quality 
monitoring data from January 2015 through December 2017 at each 
eligible monitoring site. On April 5, 2022, the EPA finalized a finding 
of failure to attain (FFA) for the Sullivan County Area, effective May 
5, 2022, in which the Agency determined that the Area did not attain 
the 1-hour SO
2
 standard by October 4, 2018.\19\
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    \19\ See 87 FR 19645 (Apr. 5, 2022).
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    The EPA's FFA triggered a requirement pursuant to CAA section 
179(d) for Tennessee to submit to the EPA a revised nonattainment SIP 
for the Sullivan County Area, within one year of the FFA publication in 
the Federal Register (i.e., by April 5, 2023), that provided for 
attainment of the 2010 SO
2
 standard as expeditiously as 
practicable but no later than five years from the FFA's Federal 
Register publication date (i.e., April 5, 2027).
    In response to the EPA's April 5, 2022, FFA, TDEC submitted a 
revised nonattainment SIP (second nonattainment SIP) on February 9, 
2023, which provided for modeled attainment of the 2010 SO
2

NAAQS based on enforceable control measures for the three coal-fired 
boilers at Eastman established in SIP operating permit No. 080222. 
Additionally, the February 9, 2023, nonattainment SIP included existing 
SO
2
 emission limits for other Eastman sources and Primester 
as measures to be adopted into the SIP.
    On June 18, 2025, TDEC submitted a request to the EPA to 
redesignate the Sullivan County Area from nonattainment to attainment, 
with an accompanying SIP revision consisting of a maintenance plan for 
the Area. The submission also included source-specific SO
2

permitted limits for two facilities in the Area, other control 
measures, and provisions for RACM and RACT that are being proposed for 
approval and incorporation into the SIP. Tennessee supplemented the 
June 18, 2025, submission on January 27, 2026 and May 20, 2026, 
providing corrections and clarifications to portions of the SIP 
narrative and attachments and further clarified its submission via 
email on August 20, 2026. The EPA is proposing to approve elements of 
Tennessee's February 9, 2023, second nonattainment SIP and Tennessee's 
June 18, 2025, submission, as supplemented on January 27, 2026 and May 
20, 2026, and clarified on August 20, 2026, as discussed in further 
detail below.

[[Page 68070]]

III. Nonattainment Planning and Redesignation

A. Requirements for SO2 Nonattainment Areas

    All States must submit SIPs or SIP revisions to show they have the 
basic air quality management program components in place to implement a 
new or revised NAAQS, as specified in CAA section 110(a)(1). These 
plans are called ``infrastructure SIPs.'' For areas designated 
nonattainment for a specific NAAQS, States must also submit 
``nonattainment plans'' that outline strategies and emissions control 
measures and demonstrate how the area will improve in air quality as 
well as attain and maintain the NAAQS.\20\
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    \20\ See CAA section 172(c).
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    Under CAA sections 110(a)(1) and (2), States are required to submit 
``infrastructure SIPs'' to ensure that they have the basic air quality 
management program components in place to provide for implementation, 
maintenance, and enforcement of the NAAQS, including the 2010 1-hour 
SO
2
 NAAQS. The EPA approved Tennessee's infrastructure SIP 
for the 2010 1-hour SO
2
 NAAQS.\21\ For the 2010 1-hour 
SO
2
 NAAQS, Tennessee's infrastructure SIP addressed CAA 
sections 110(a)(2)(A) through (H) and (J) through (M), except 
110(a)(2)(C) to the extent that subsection refers to a permit program 
as required in part D, title I of the CAA, i.e., nonattainment new 
source review (NNSR). CAA sections 110(a)(2)(I) and (K), which 
specifically address the nonattainment plan provisions, are addressed 
in section V.B of this NPRM.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    \21\ See 81 FR 85410 (Nov. 28, 2016), 83 FR 48237 (Sept. 24, 
2018), and 88 FR 53800 (Aug. 9, 2023).
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    CAA section 110(l) contains two main provisions applicable to SIPs, 
including nonattainment plans. First, CAA section 110(l) requires that 
each SIP revision submitted by a State must be adopted by a State after 
reasonable notice and public hearing. Second, under CAA section 110(l), 
the EPA may not approve a SIP if it would interfere with any applicable 
requirement concerning NAAQS attainment, reasonable further progress 
toward attainment, or any other applicable requirement of the CAA. For 
the reasons discussed in section V.D of this NPRM, the EPA is proposing 
that Tennessee has met these requirements.
    Nonattainment plans must meet the applicable requirements of the 
CAA, specifically CAA title I, section 110 and part D. To address plan 
requirements for nonattainment areas, there are two elements of CAA 
section 110(a)(2) pertaining to part D in title I of the CAA that are 
outside the scope of infrastructure SIPs. The first is CAA section 
110(a)(2)(C) to the extent it refers to NNSR under part D of title I of 
the CAA, and the second is CAA section 110(a)(2)(I) in its 
entirety.\22\ For the first of these two elements, the EPA approved 
Tennessee's SIP revisions comprising the State's rules for NNSR most 
recently on July 30, 2012.\23\ For the second of these two elements, 
the EPA's ``SIP Lean Toolkit for Collaboration Between EPA and Air 
Agencies,'' December 6, 2019 (2019 SIP Lean Toolkit) \24\ identifies 
CAA sections 172, 191, and 192 as the applicable planning requirements 
specific to SO
2
 nonattainment areas.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    \22\ See Guidance on Infrastructure State Implementation Plan 
(SIP) Elements under Clean Air Act Sections 110(a)(1) and 110(a)(2); 
EPA, Sep. 13, 2013, can be found at 
https://www.epa.gov/sites/default/files/2015-12/documents/guidance_on_infrastructure_sip_elements_multipollutant_final_sept_2013.pdf
 at p. 4, available in the docket for this action.
    \23\ See 77 FR 44481 (July 30, 2012).
    \24\ 
https://www.epa.gov/sites/default/files/2019-12/documents/sip_lean_toolkit_for_collaboration_between_epa_and_air_agencies.pdf

at pp. 22-23.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    In areas designated as nonattainment for a particular NAAQS, CAA 
section 172 includes nonattainment plan provisions that require States 
to submit SIPs that demonstrate the affected area will attain the 
relevant NAAQS as expeditiously as practicable, but no later than the 
applicable statutory attainment date. To support such an attainment 
demonstration for SO
2
 nonattainment plans, the EPA's 2019 
SIP Lean Toolkit specifies the applicable provisions of the CAA as 
sections 172(a)(2), (b), (c)(1) through (c)(6), and (c)(9). As 
discussed in section V.B of this NPRM, the EPA is proposing to find 
that Tennessee's 2023 second nonattainment plan meets each of these 
applicable provisions of CAA section 172.
    CAA section 191(a) directs States to submit SIPs to the EPA for 
areas designated as nonattainment with respect to the primary NAAQS for 
sulfur oxides, nitrogen dioxide, or lead within 18 months of the 
effective date of the designation. As noted above, on March 18, 2016, 
the EPA determined that Tennessee failed to submit a complete SIP 
within 18 months of the effective designation of the Sullivan County 
Area to nonattainment. TDEC initially submitted a May 12, 2017, 
attainment SIP following the FFS. CAA section 192(a) requires that SIPs 
for nonattainment areas must provide for attainment of the relevant 
NAAQS as expeditiously as practicable, but no later than five years 
from the effective date of the nonattainment designation. However, on 
April 5, 2022, the EPA determined that the State failed to attain by 
the applicable attainment date, triggering a requirement under CAA 
section 179(d) to submit a SIP revision by April 5, 2023 including 
``such additional measures as the Administrator may reasonably 
prescribe, including all measures that can be feasibly implemented in 
the area in light of technological achievability, costs, and any nonair 
quality and other air quality-related health and environmental 
impacts'' and which would provide for attainment by April 5, 2027.\25\ 
As discussed in section V.B of this NPRM, Tennessee's 2023 second 
nonattainment SIP includes an attainment demonstration for the Sullivan 
County Nonattainment Area that demonstrated attainment of the 2010 1-
hour SO
2
 NAAQS as expeditiously as practicable, by the date 
of the June 18, 2025, redesignation request and maintenance plan, and 
in less than five years from the Apri 5, 2022, publication date.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    \25\ The EPA did not prescribe additional measures under CAA 
section 179(d)(2) at the time of the finding.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

B. Criteria for Redesignation

    The CAA provides the requirements for redesignating a nonattainment 
area to attainment. Specifically, CAA section 107(d)(3)(E) allows for 
redesignation provided that: (1) the Administrator determines that the 
area has attained the applicable NAAQS; (2) the Administrator has fully 
approved the applicable implementation plan for the area under CAA 
section 110(k); (3) the Administrator determines that the improvement 
in air quality is due to permanent and enforceable reductions in 
emissions resulting from implementation of the applicable SIP and 
applicable Federal air pollutant control regulations, and other 
permanent and enforceable reductions; (4) the Administrator has fully 
approved a maintenance plan for the area as meeting the requirements of 
CAA section 175A; and (5) the State containing such an area has met all 
requirements applicable to the area for the purposes of redesignation 
under CAA section 110 and part D.

nonattainment area for the 2010 SO

paragraphs. A more detailed discussion of TDEC's modeling can be found 
in the EPA's Sullivan County SO

    TDEC's modeling analysis was developed in accordance with the EPA's 
Guideline on Air Quality Models (Modeling Guideline) \92\ and the 
Modeling Guidance provided in appendix A of the EPA's SO
2

Nonattainment Area Guidance. The modeling was performed using the EPA's 
preferred air dispersion modeling system--the American Meteorological 
Society/Environmental Protection Agency Regulatory Model (AERMOD)--
consisting of the AERMOD (version 22112) air dispersion model \93\ and 
multiple data input preprocessors as described below.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

on the November 29, 2024, final Appendix W revision rule, see 

https://www.epa.gov/scram/2024-appendix-w-final-rule

the time the modeling was performed by TDEC in 2023.

    TDEC used regulatory default options in the AERMOD modeling. Based 
upon an evaluation of the land use within three kilometers of Eastman, 
more than 50 percent of the land use is classified under urban land use 
categories rather than rural land use categories. Therefore, urban 
dispersion coefficients were used in the modeling. Due to the larger 
amount of heat released from Eastman, although the facility is located 
in a city with a population of about 50,000, a surrogate population 
value of 200,000 was calculated by Eastman for use with the urban 
option in AERMOD as the ``effective population.'' Additional details 
about the procedures used for the urban option are provided in the 
EPA's Sullivan County SO
2
 Modeling TSD.
    AERMET and AERMINUTE are data pre-processors for the EPA's AERMOD 
air quality dispersion model, generating meteorological observations 
and wind data information, respectively. AERMET (version 22112) and 
AERMINUTE (version 15272) were used to process one year (April 2012-
March 2013) of site-specific meteorological data \94\ (wind speed and 
direction, temperature, and turbulence parameters), collected at a 100-
meter tower equipped with a Sound Detection and Ranging (SODAR) wind 
profiler system specifically installed near Eastman for this modeling 
analysis. Additional meteorology inputs needed for AERMOD that were not 
collected at the site-specific meteorology station (e.g., cloud cover 
data) were obtained from the Bristol/Johnson/Kingsport, Tri-Cities 
Regional Airport (KTRI) National Weather Service (NWS) automated 
surface observing system (ASOS) station (WBAN No. 13877), in 
combination with twice daily upper-air meteorological soundings from 
the Nashville, Tennessee NWS station (WBAN No. 13897). The Tri-Cities 
Regional Airport is located approximately 8.5 miles east/southeast of 
Eastman, and the Nashville Airport is located approximately 200 miles 
west of Kingsport, but it has mean mixing heights comparable to the 
Kingsport area. The pre-processor AERSURFACE (version 20060) was used 
to process 2011 National Land Cover Database (NLCD) data to derive the 
albedo, Bowen ratio, and surface roughness surface characteristics 
needed for AERMET.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    \94\ As discussed in Section 8.4.2.e of the EPA's Guideline on 
Air Quality Models in 40 CFR part 51, Appendix W, if at least 1-year 
of site-specific meteorology data is available, it is preferred for 
use in air quality modeling analyses. Prior to the data being 
collected by Eastman in 2012-2013, Eastman and TDEC consulted with 
the EPA about using a partial year in 2012 and partial year in 2013 
to meet the 1-year of site-specific data requirement. The EPA 
concurred that it was not necessary for the 1-year of data to 
correspond to a single calendar-year (January-December). The April 
2012-March 2013 site-specific data continues to be the best 
available wind, temperature and turbulence data for the modeling 
analysis because data for these parameters from the nearby Tri-
Cities Regional Airport NWS site is located outside the river valley 
where Eastman is located, so the parameters measured at the airport 
are not representative of the conditions at the facility location.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    The pre-processor AERMAP (version 18081) was used to generate 
terrain inputs for the receptors, based on a digital elevation mapping 
database from the National Elevation Dataset developed by the U.S. 
Geological Survey. Model receptors were placed at 50-meter intervals 
along the fence-line, public access roads, and riverbanks as well as in 
a 100-meter grid throughout the remainder of the three-km non-
attainment area (excluding the area inside the Eastman fence-line 
because access is controlled by fences, gates, and other restrictions

the EPA has required certain States to establish programs to address

requirements for a State are not linked with a particular nonattainment 
area's designation and classification in that State. The transport SIP 
submission requirements, where applicable, continue to apply to a State 
regardless of the designation of any one area in the State. As a

which are linked with a particular area's designation and

VII. Statutory and Executive Order Reviews

    Under the CAA, the Administrator is required to approve a SIP 
submission that complies with the provisions of the Act and applicable 
Federal regulations.\131\ Thus, in reviewing SIP submissions, the EPA's 
role is to approve State choices, provided that they meet the criteria 
of the CAA. Accordingly, these proposed actions merely propose to 
approve State law as meeting Federal requirements and do not impose 
additional requirements beyond those imposed by State law. Furthermore, 
redesignation of an area to attainment and the accompanying approval of 
a maintenance plan under section 107(d)(3)(E) are actions that affect 
the status of a geographical area and do not impose any additional 
regulatory requirements on sources beyond those imposed by State law. A 
redesignation to attainment does not in and of itself create any new 
requirements, but rather results in the applicability of requirements 
contained in the CAA for areas that have been redesignated to 
attainment. For these reasons, these proposed actions:
